description: Machine-readable taxonomy for the claim-audit-lab 5-label framework. Inspired in spirit (not in operational rule) by GRADE's downgrade/upgrade pattern; here downgrades are explicit and asymmetric, and the framework itself is registered as an [Open conjecture] (see methodology/README.md Section 0).

labels.definition: Exact-by-construction (algebraic identity, integer arithmetic), or directly measured with a pre-registered, reproducible harness whose seed/config/output are committed.
preconditions: the assertion reduces to a finite check that any reader can rerun
examples: ladder rule e = round((N-1)/phi^2) reproduces 9/9 realised GF format widths
Wikipedia BLP edit reverts within median 5 minutes (documented in academic study)

downgrade_factors.trigger: a free parameter is chosen post-hoc to make the identity hold
the harness exists but the reader cannot reproduce because seed/config/output are not committed

labels.definition: Matches data but with at least one post-hoc parameter, OR a matched-k situation where k was chosen to make the fit work, OR a measurement without pre-registered held-out test.
preconditions: the fit is real (no fabrication or arithmetic error)
but at least one degree of freedom was set after seeing the data, or the cardinality of the search space is not stated
examples: factor-3 ASHA schedule in IGLA (geometric scheduling is standard; the choice of 3 is an empirical fit)
alpha^-1 closed-form within X ppm given M post-hoc free coefficients

downgrade_factors.trigger: the search space cardinality is large enough that the look-elsewhere correction (Gross-Vitells) eliminates significance
a falsification path is stated and the matter is unresolved

labels.upgrade_path_to_verified: pre-register a held-out test, run, and lock the seed/config; if it holds on the held-out data without further tuning, promote to [Verified]

labels.definition: Plausible, mathematically or empirically motivated, and explicitly carrying a falsification path (Fpath) that any reader can in principle execute.
preconditions: the claim is stated precisely enough that a reader can name what would falsify it
the Fpath is recorded inline OR in a falsification ledger row
no post-hoc parameter that has not been disclosed
examples: GoldenFloat ladder's breadth-as-moat (FL-002 ledger row, Fpath = a posit/takum/MX ladder matches at matched bit budgets)
phi-canonical AdamW beats tuned standard AdamW at champion budget (Phase B1-real ablation pending)

downgrade_factors.trigger: the Fpath is stated but unexecutable, or a control already matches and the result is not recorded
weak venue (vanity press, predatory journal) AND no independent replication

labels.upgrade_path_to_verified: execute the Fpath; if the conjecture survives a pre-registered, well-powered test with no matched-k ambiguity, promote to [Verified]

labels.definition: Fails one or more of: (a) no stated Fpath, (b) no look-elsewhere correction over the search space, (c) a documented control already matches, (d) venue weakness (single-source, non-peer-reviewed, or platform with known issues).
preconditions: the claim is published or publicly defended
at least one of (a)-(d) is documented in the case file
examples: El Naschie's E-infinity constants without symmetric look-elsewhere accounting [Risk via (b) and (d)]
phi-specificity for IGLA after control-grammar test failed [Risk via (c), via Pellis-Vasilev-Olsen paper Section 4]

downgrade_factors.trigger: two or more of (a)-(d) apply simultaneously
the author or publisher formally withdraws

labels.upgrade_path_to_open_conjecture: state the Fpath, apply the look-elsewhere correction, and (if applicable) move the claim to a peer-reviewed venue; this is the standard rehabilitation path

labels.definition: Two or more [Risk] factors apply simultaneously, OR a single factor of extreme severity (e.g. a long history of formal retractions on directly comparable claims).
preconditions: OR a documented pattern of prior retractions in the same programme
examples: self-citation rate >50% in a programme with multiple journal retractions
claim that matches a programme already cited in Wikipedia's WP:FRINGE noticeboard
labels.upgrade_path_to_risk: respond to one of the stacked factors with documented evidence (e.g. an independent replication, a venue change, a published look-elsewhere analysis)

labels.definition: A formal retraction notice has been issued by the author, the publisher, or the journal. Recorded as [Retracted] strictly on the basis of that notice, NOT on the basis of inferred misconduct.
preconditions: a citable retraction notice exists (URL, DOI, or journal statement)
OR the author has issued a public withdrawal that is archivable
examples: delta_CP = 3/phi^2 prediction withdrawn by Vasilev (FL ledger, internal)
El Naschie's papers retracted from Chaos, Solitons and Fractals post-2009 by the new editorial board
labels.rehabilitation_path: [Retracted] is final for the specific publication that was withdrawn. A new submission of a related claim restarts at the appropriate label (most commonly [Risk] given the prior history).

framework_self_label.label: open_conjecture
framework_self_label.Fpath: the framework is falsified if an outside reviewer demonstrates that two or more labels collapse in practice (e.g. [Risk] and [High-risk] are not reliably distinguishable across blind raters), OR if the framework systematically misclassifies a well-bounded positive control (CASE-05 Kramer-Klimesch, CASE-06 de Groot serve this role)
framework_self_label.rationale: Laudan (1983) refuted the strong demarcation criterion; any 5-label taxonomy that pretends to be exact-by-construction is itself making a claim that needs the same falsifiability discipline it imposes on others. See methodology/README.md Section 0.

cross_references.note: GRADE downgrades the strength of evidence by named factors (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias). Our downgrade_factors borrow the asymmetric explicit-factor pattern but NOT the operational thresholds; GRADE's domain is clinical trials with statistical power, ours is heterogeneous claim auditing.

Cochrane uses Low / Some concerns / High risk per signalling-question domain. Our [Verified] / [Open conjecture] / [Risk] / [High-risk] mirrors that gradient but our domains are framework-level (a)-(d) rather than per-trial.
Falsification path is mandatory; the framework itself is held to the same Fpath rule (see framework_self_label).

cross_references.external: Laudan (1983), 'The Demise of the Demarcation Problem'
cross_references.note: Forces this framework to refuse the demarcation tokens listed in FRAMEWORK.md as labels; we use [Risk] and [High-risk] with named factors instead.
